# package discovery

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/discovery"
```

Package discovery finds VTNs on the local network, and lets a VTN be found, with DNS-SD over Multicast DNS as OpenADR 3.1.0 describes it ("Discovery and Configuration of Local VTNs"): the service type is \_openadr3.\_tcp, and a TXT record carries the version, the base path and URL of the API, the program names and whether the VTN authenticates.

A VEN at a customer site looks for the gateway there:

	vtns, err := discovery.Browse(ctx, discovery.Options{})
	for _, vtn := range vtns {
		fmt.Println(vtn.Instance, vtn.URL(), vtn.RequiresAuth)
	}

and a VTN announces itself for as long as it runs:

	ad, err := discovery.Advertise(discovery.Advertisement{Port: 8443, BasePath: "openadr3"})
	defer ad.Close()

Multicast DNS tells nothing about who answers: anyone on the link can claim to be a VTN. What a VEN finds this way is an address to try, and the TLS certificate of the VTN, and the VEN's credentials, are what make it trustworthy, as for an address from any other source.

The package speaks Multicast DNS over IPv4. It announces the IPv6 addresses of the host as well, and reports those of the VTNs it finds.

## Types

### type Advertisement

```go
type Advertisement struct {
	// Instance names the VTN to people, such as "Building 4 VTN". It has
	// to be unique on the network; "OpenADR 3 VTN" when empty.
	Instance string
	// Host is the host name to announce, without ".local"; the name of
	// the machine when empty.
	Host string
	// Port is the port the API is served at. Required.
	Port int
	// BasePath is what comes before the paths of the API, such as
	// "openadr3", when it is not served at the root.
	BasePath string
	// Version is the OpenADR version; "3.1.0" when empty.
	Version string
	// LocalURL is the URL of the API. When empty it is https, the host
	// with ".local", the port and the base path.
	LocalURL string
	// ProgramNames are the names of the programs meant for local VENs.
	ProgramNames []string
	// NoAuth announces a VTN that serves clients without a token (see
	// Config.AllowAnonymous of package server). The default announces one
	// that requires authentication.
	NoAuth bool
	// OpenAPIURL is where the VTN serves its OpenAPI document, if it does.
	OpenAPIURL string
	// Logger receives failures to send. Nil disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger

}
```

Advertisement is what a VTN announces on the local network.

### type Advertiser

```go
type Advertiser struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Advertiser answers the queries of the local network for a VTN, until it is closed.

#### func Advertise

```go
func Advertise(a Advertisement) (*Advertiser, error)
```

Advertise starts announcing a VTN on every network interface that has multicast. It fails when there is none, or when port 5353 cannot be shared with the resolver of the system.

It does not probe for the names first: an instance or host name that another machine on the network already uses is not detected.

#### func (Advertiser) Close

```go
func (ad *Advertiser) Close() error
```

Close takes the announcement back and stops answering.

### type Options

```go
type Options struct {
	// Timeout is how long to wait for VTNs to answer; 3 seconds when zero.
	// The context given to Browse can end the wait earlier.

}
```

Options decide how Browse looks.

### type VTN

```go
type VTN struct {
	// Instance is the name of the service instance, such as "My VTN".
	Instance string
	// Host is the host name of the VTN, such as "myvtn.local", and Port
	// the port of its API.
	Host string
	Port int
	// Addrs are the addresses the VTN announced for Host. The
	// specification asks a VEN to prefer the name, because addresses
	// change; they are for a system that cannot resolve .local names.
	Addrs []netip.Addr
	// Version is the OpenADR version, such as "3.1.0".
	Version string
	// BasePath is what comes before the paths of the API, such as
	// "openadr3/3.1.0".
	BasePath string
	// LocalURL is the URL of the API as the VTN gives it.
	LocalURL string
	// ProgramNames are the programs meant for local VENs.
	ProgramNames []string
	// RequiresAuth says the VTN wants a token. It is false only for a VTN
	// that says so.
	RequiresAuth bool
	// OpenAPIURL is where the VTN serves its OpenAPI document.
	OpenAPIURL string
	// Text holds every key of the TXT record, in lower case, including
	// those above and any the specification does not name.
	Text map[string]string
}
```

VTN is a VTN as it announces itself.

#### func Browse

```go
func Browse(ctx context.Context, o Options) ([]VTN, error)
```

Browse asks the local network for VTNs and returns those that answered within the timeout, by instance name. Finding none is not an error.

It asks in both ways there are. As a one-shot resolver (RFC 6762, section 5.1), from a port of its own, to which a responder answers directly: that needs nothing but a socket, and works beside the resolver of the system. And, where the Multicast DNS port can be shared, as a Multicast DNS querier, from that port, hearing what is answered to the whole network: some responders, OpenLEADR's among them, answer no other way. A machine on which the port cannot be shared still finds the responders that answer directly.

#### func (VTN) URL

```go
func (v VTN) URL() string
```

URL returns the base URL of the VTN's API: LocalURL when the VTN gave one, and otherwise https, the host, the port and the base path.
